claims.text: Dynamic tensile loading induces localized compositional heterogeneities in CoCrFeNi nanopillars.
The dynamically induced compositional heterogeneities temporarily reduce the generalized stacking fault energy.
Reduced generalized stacking fault energy facilitates deformation twinning.
Reduced generalized stacking fault energy facilitates dislocation glide.
Dynamic loading causes simultaneous, spatially coordinated activation of deformation twinning and dislocation slip.
Coordinated twinning and dislocation slip promote a more homogeneous strain distribution.
Coordinated twinning and dislocation slip delay necking.
Delayed necking produces an enhanced strength–ductility balance relative to quasi-static loading.
Dynamically deformed nanopillars will have a significantly higher twin density than quasi-statically deformed nanopillars.
Dynamically deformed nanopillars will have a more uniform dislocation distribution than quasi-statically deformed nanopillars.
Dynamic loading will increase flow stress relative to quasi-static loading.
Dynamic loading will produce super-elongation relative to quasi-static loading.
Traditional dislocation slip dominates quasi-static deformation of the baseline CoCrFeNi nanopillars.
Quasi-statically loaded nanopillars have lower twin densities than dynamically loaded nanopillars.
Quasi-statically loaded nanopillars neck earlier than dynamically loaded nanopillars.
The proposed mechanism is expected to apply to single-crystalline CoCrFeNi nanopillars deformed at room temperature across controlled strain-rate variations.
